transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendes (Nimbus Lead Eng), Aisha Rahman (Nimbus PM), Ben Holt (Nimbus SRE), Samir (data eng)

Summary: quick recap, then deep dive into invoke orchestration, function calling, structured outputs and failure modes; ended with concrete next steps and security follow-up.

[00:00] Jordan: ok, hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda: we want to review the pilot results from last week, talk through the invoke orchestration decision flow you implemented, and dig into the serialization mismatch you reported. priya will run through the tech details.

[00:18] Priya (SE): yeah hi, thanks. i pulled logs from the sandbox; we saw about 120ms median token latency for short-turn prompts, but the decision-flow orchestration has some 2–3x variance when the function calling path triggers additional tools. so, basically, normal output paths are fine, but when you hit the toolchain we observed spikes.

[00:46] Carlos: yes, that's what we saw in staging too. when the flow calls the patient-data lookup tool, sometimes the payload came back as a stringified json blob — like double-encoded — and our SDK's parser choked. i think that's the serialization mismatch you mentioned.

[01:10] Priya: mhm, we traced that to the function-calling wrapper in the app. two possibilities: either the app is passing a pre-serialized string into the functions field, or the runtime's structured-output marshaler is returning a string for complex nested objects. could be a schema mismatch.

[01:35] Ben (SRE): also, on the infra side, we saw queuing on small bursts. looks like we need smarter batching policy when there's a mix of short inline completions and longer tool-invoked calls. the batcher groups by arrival but not by expected token length right now.

[02:01] Jordan: right, so tradeoff there is latency vs cost. if we keep tiny batches for latency, cost goes up. if we batch more aggressively we can lower token cost but micro-latency increases. priya, can you sketch the change we recommend?

[02:20] Priya: recommendation is workload-aware batching: route tool-calling requests to a separate queue with a slightly larger max latency SLO (100–200ms headroom) and keep non-tool short completions on the low-latency path. this is something Redwood's runtime supports via routing policies; we can configure on the pilot cluster.

[02:45] Carlos: would that require Dedicated? we're trying to understand whether this is achievable on hosted.

[02:54] Jordan: you can do this on hosted by config (route to different model variants / priority queues) but Dedicated gives you strict isolation and predictable throughput; hosted can still do smart routing but noisy neighbors are a factor. for the pilot, we can apply the routing policy in hosted to emulate the dedicated behavior and run benchmarks.

[03:18] Aisha (PM): from product perspective, reliability during the decision flow is more important than micro-latency for many of our user journeys. so pushing for stability first makes sense. cost is still a concern though.

[03:35] Priya: noted. about the serialization: one quick mitigation is to enforce a strict structured-output contract at the SDK layer: force objects in the functions response to be returned as native JSON, validate on receipt, and fail fast with a clear error. i can push a small SDK patch that adds stricter parsing and clearer errors.

[03:58] Carlos: that would help. we did find a couple of places in our code where we call JSON.stringify() before passing the payload to the SDK — that's our bug. we'll clean that up but we also want the SDK to be more defensive.

[04:15] Priya: good, do that and send the sample failing payloads; we'll add unit tests to the SDK to catch those. also we'll include a small validation helper you can call pre-send.

[04:28] Ben: one other thing — the KV cache behavior. when we run the decision flow repeatedly for the same patient, the KV cache sometimes returns stale entries during rollouts. there's a TTL mismatch between our client-side cache and Redwood's prefix caching.

[04:48] Priya: ah yes, TTLs. currently our prefix/KV caching defaults to a 5 minute TTL for the pilot. we can expose the TTL and make it configurable per-route, or add cache-busting options in your SDK to force a fresh lookup.

[05:02] Samir: we'd prefer configurable TTL per route. some patient lookups are ephemeral and should be 30s; others can be 10min.

[05:12] Jordan: that's easy — we'll surface route-level cache TTL in the console and via the SDK. i'll note that as a follow-up.

[05:22] Aisha: back to the benchmarks — what metrics are you going to run? we need throughput, p95/p99 latency, cost-per-1000-requests, and error rates for the function-calling path.

[05:34] Priya: yes — we'll run two profiles: 1) mixed workload (70% short completions, 30% tool-calls) and 2) heavy tool-calling (50% multi-step invokes). we'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail jitter, tokens per second, and cost estimates comparing hosted vs a simulated Dedicated reservation.

[05:58] Carlos: can you also include cases with KV cache warm vs cold? that affects latency a lot.

[06:05] Priya: absolutely. we'll include warm/cold cache scenarios and prefix caching impact.

[06:12] Jordan: great. security question — Nimbus is going to need KMS integration and audit logs for the pilot. where are we on that?

[06:22] Marta (CSM): we have a SOC2 pack and an architecture note. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we can integrate with your cloud KMS in certain regions and provide audit logs via our console or a log export. i'll schedule a separate security deep-dive with your security team next week.

[06:40] Aisha: do we get event-level audit trails for function invocations? we need to show which model version and which tool was invoked for compliance.

[06:49] Marta: yes — the platform emits per-request metadata: model id, model version, route id, and tool-invoke events. we keep a configurable retention window. for enterprise we can increase retention or export to your SIEM.

[07:05] Ben: how granular are the logs? we need to avoid PII in the logs — can we redact before export?

[07:12] Marta: you can enable redaction at the route level; the SDK also supports client-side PII redaction helpers. we'll include guidance in the security doc.

[07:25] Priya: circling back to function-calling errors: we saw one replay where the runtime retried a tool call and the downstream idempotency key was missing, creating duplicate side-effects. recommend you add idempotency tokens to tool calls and we can add a runtime-side guard.

[07:45] Carlos: good catch. our data pipeline needs that; we'll add idempotency keys.

[07:52] Jordan: ok, on structured-output stability, you asked about enforcement and schema evolution. Priya?

[08:00] Priya: we suggest three layers: 1) schema at the prompt level (examples + json-schema), 2) SDK validation on response parse, 3) runtime regression alerts — Redwood Optimize can run evals against a prompt-set and alert on schema drift or quality regressions. for the pilot we'll set up a small eval set to detect regressions on the decision-flow outputs.

[08:24] Aisha: how quickly can we get those regression alerts? we want to be notified if a change increases error rates above 2% for critical flows.

[08:33] Priya: we can configure thresholds and email/Slack alerts. realistic detection with 95% confidence for small samples will take a day of traffic, but for the pilot we can run synthetic checks after each deploy.

[08:48] Carlos: synthetic checks sound good. also, can Redwood Optimize suggest quantization or model variant adjustments if we want to cut costs?

[08:56] Priya: yes — Optimize will analyze token distribution and latency and recommend quantization profiles or smaller model families for non-critical steps. for example, you could run a cheaper model for a pre-filter step and a larger model only for the final response generation.

[09:14] Ben: any concern about output drift if we use mixed models in the decision flow? we need consistent semantics.

[09:22] Priya: that's the main risk — we recommend running an acceptance test suite for each step that validates semantics (e.g., medical entity extraction parity) before switching model variants. Optimize can flag regressions, but you'll want unit tests too.

[09:38] Jordan: ok, next up: timeline and pilot extension. Carlos, you mentioned wanting a two-week extension to run the test matrix?

[09:46] Carlos: yes, we need two more weeks to finish end-to-end validation, and potentially run a Dedicated proof-of-concept if the hosted configs don't meet SLOs.

[09:55] Jordan: sounds reasonable. i'll get pricing for a short Dedicated reservation and a hosted pilot extension. expect a sheet by tomorrow.

[10:04] Aisha: please include the cost delta and the expected p95 improvement for Dedicated. that's a key input for our execs.

[10:12] Jordan: will do.

[10:16] Priya: quick note on SDK versions — we noticed some apps are on 0.9.x and the newer 1.x SDK has the structured-output helpers and better retry semantics. we recommend upgrading to 1.0.3 in staging; we can provide a migration guide.

[10:30] Samir: any breaking changes we should be aware of?

[10:33] Priya: minimal — mostly opt-in helpers. we'll send the migration notes and a small compatibility shim.

[10:40] Carlos: ok good. last thing — samples. we'll share the 500 structured examples today. expect them in the shared folder.

[10:48] Jordan: perfect. recap of next steps: priya runs the benchmarks (hosted + simulated Dedicated), mart schedules the security deep-dive and attaches SOC2 docs, carlos shares schema/examples, jordan sends pricing. action items on the doc.

[11:05] Aisha: thanks everyone. quick question — for the benchmark, can you also include a run with function-calling disabled as a baseline?

[11:12] Priya: yes, baseline run without function calls included.

[11:20] Jordan: great — we'll follow up with a results email and a screen share demo of the runtime tuning options once benchmarks are complete. thanks all.

End of transcript.
